verdict.rationale: OpenClaw documents built-in sandboxing that runs tool execution inside a sandbox backend to limit blast radius, with configurable modes, scopes, workspace access and images. Separately, an optional Docker setup gives an isolated, throwaway Gateway environment, and multi-agent and fleet cells each get their own workspace, state and credentials, so testing can be kept away from the real setup. Community remarks comparing the security model to running as root are general skepticism, not a concrete failure of the sandbox. Missing for 10: explicit docs on a dedicated test/staging-vs-production data workflow, guarantees that sandboxed runs cannot reach production credentials or data, and independent hands-on corroboration that the sandbox isolation works.
